title: Free Payout Allowance on Paloma Business Accounts
content:
At the start of every billing period a Paloma Business account is granted its plan's free payouts for the period.

### The rule

1. A local-rail payout uses one free payout whenever free payouts remaining is above 0 at its submission, in submission order, and then carries no payout fee.
2. SWIFT payouts never use the allowance.
3. Because no plan carries unused free payouts forward, free payouts still unused at the end of the period lapse when the next period starts.
4. A free payout is restored only when the payout that used it is cancelled before release within the same billing period. A payout cancelled in a later period, or returned after release, does not restore it. The test reads the payout's reference, the date its free payout was used and the start of the current billing period, all from the system records.
5. The allowance of a plan change applies from the next period's grant.

### Period cases (hypothetical, a plan granting 10 free payouts)

| Situation | Effect on the allowance |
|---|---|
| Ten local-rail payouts submitted, then an eleventh | The first ten each use one free payout; the eleventh finds none remaining and does not use one |
| A SWIFT payout submitted with free payouts remaining | No free payout used |
| A local-rail payout that used a free payout is cancelled before release in the same billing period | The free payout is restored |
| The same payout is cancelled after the next billing period has started | Not restored |
| A payout that used a free payout is returned by the beneficiary bank after release | Not restored |
| Three free payouts unused when the next period starts | The three lapse; the new period starts with its own grant |
| The account moves to a plan with a larger allowance mid-period | The larger allowance applies from the next period's grant |
